title.narrative: Output 7.1. Increased capacity of the member States to ensure respect for, promote and realize fundamental principles and rights at work

description.narrative:
In 2020, the Minister of Manpower issued Decree NO. 35 to establish the National Steering Committee (NSC) to achieve the National Action Plan for Combating the Worst Forms of Child Labour in Egypt (2018 – 2025) (NAP). The role of the NAP NSC is to coordinate all the national activities and monitor child labour in collaboration with the Ministry of Manpower (MOM). Two online tripartite NSC meetings took place to discuss the progress in implementing the NAP and validate the hazardous work list for children. Two in-person meetings took place to validate the amendments of the Child Code and introducing the child labour monitoring system.
Seven individualized annual implementation plans to activate the role of the national stakeholders in the implementation of the NAP were drafted, validated, approved and are currently being implemented.
The ministerial decree no. 118 of 2003 on the hazardous worklist for children was updated and validated by the tripartite constituents and issued as decree no. 215 in 2021 by MOM. The updates will provide the legal framework towards a safer work environment for children.
Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work (FPRW), with special focus on combating child labour, were mainstreamed in the Labour and Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) national inspection checklists to better identify, report and refer child labour cases in addition to ensure better working conditions for apprentices in compliance with national relevant labour laws and regulations. With support from the government of the Netherlands, the ILO provided technical support to the Ministry of Manpower to improve the legal framework for protecting children from child labour, including the updating of the hazardous worklist for children, and the labour and OSH inspection checklists. It also provided technical support to the national stakeholders to effectively undertake their roles in implementation of the NAP
In addition, the ILO: - facilitated a tripartite validation workshop on the hazardous worklist for children; - provided training on the updated OSH inspection checklist for 115 inspectors in its 5 targeted governorates; and - facilitated the 4 tripartite NSC meetings since its establishment.
